messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — GPU pool eu-west-1/hotshard-3 is reporting sustained queue growth and >95% evictions. Autoscaler attempted scale x3 but no new nodes accepted. Throttling increased across affected routes. Paging oncall. <https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd123/gpu-pool?orgId=1|metrics>
Anna (oncall): I'm on it, ACKing the page. Does anyone have a quick summary of customer-facing impact?
Matt (sre): Seeing queue length climb from ~200 -> 3.2k over the last 8m. p99 latency spiked to 4.2s, throttles up 14%. Hotshard-3 is at 100% GPU memory, OOM-style evictions. Autoscaler logs show scale requests failing with zone quota errors:
```
ERROR autoscaler: scale up failed: InsufficientCapacity: Requested instances exceed quota for eu-west-1
request_id=xyz-123
```
Ravi (infra): Confirmed. Cloud account quota for GPUs in eu-west-1 is at limit; we've been hitting it earlier today. There's also a new constraint from a provider maintenance window reducing available GPU inventory on that AZ.
Lee (eng-runtime): Adding what I see — reduced throughput correlates with two config changes in the last rollout: continuous_batching.window reduced from 40ms -> 10ms and kv_prefix_cache.ttl lowered from 30m -> 1m. That increases cache churn and decreases effective batching opportunities.
Sara (support): Got a spike of customer errors; support ticket stream shows 12 high-priority customers experiencing increased 429s for generation endpoints since ~10:12UTC.
Anna (oncall): Priorities: 1) Stop customer impact, 2) re-enable capacity, 3) fix config regression. Proposed live mitigations?
Matt (sre): Short-term mitigations:
- Temporarily raise autoscaler scale_cap for dedicated pools to allow cross-AZ fallback (if infra ok). Command:
```
kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"scale_cap":"20"}}'
```
- Rollback the batching change to previous window (40ms) to increase batching hit rate.
- Increase kv_prefix_cache.ttl back to 30m or flush prefix cache to avoid cold misses.
Lee (eng-runtime): I can push a rollback of batching param to stable config, but need DeployBot approval. Patch snippet:
```
continuous_batching:
  window_ms: 40
```
DeployBot: Automated change control: rollback request queued, requires two approvers. Approvers: Ravi, Matt.
Ravi (infra): Approving rollback. Also I'm opening a quota increase request with cloud provider; ETA uncertain. Meanwhile I'll enable cross-region fallback policy for critical routes.
Matt (sre): To contain immediate customer impact, suggest disabling lower-tier routes and redirect critical traffic to dedicated pools with higher SLA. I can apply a feature-flag throttle:
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/flags -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","tier":"platinum","action":"pin-to-dedicated"}'
```
Anna (oncall): Sara, can you surface a short customer impact bulletin (internal) summarizing affected customers and current mitigation state? Also please triage any escalations.
Sara (support): On it — will post an internal bulletin and ping the top 20 accounts. Draft will include ETA ranges and rollback note.
Lee (eng-runtime): Quick perf check after we roll back batching/window to 40ms: expected batching hit rate should jump from ~12% to ~58% based on recent workload profiles. That should reduce per-token load and ease GPU memory pressure.
Matt (sre): Additional ops: flush prefix cache on hotshard-3 to evict pathological entries (command below) — be careful, this can increase load transiently.
```
curl -X POST https://runtime.internal/hotshard-3/cache/flush
```
Ravi (infra): I've temporarily enabled cross-AZ fallback and bumped scale_cap to 20. Autoscaler is now able to allocate 3 extra nodes to a different AZ; provisioning in progress.
incident-bot: UPDATE — scale event succeeded, 3 instances provisioning (ids: i-0a1b2c, i-0a1b2d, i-0a1b2e). Monitoring.
Matt (sre): We're seeing queue drain begin, p95 latency falling back to 1.1s. Throttles down from 14% -> 3%.
Anna (oncall): Good. Next steps: Lee, apply batching rollback and kv_prefix_cache.ttl change. Ravi, follow up on quota increase request and provider maintenance timeline. Matt, keep metrics dashboard open and watch for evictions. Sara, update customers with a short note.
Lee (eng-runtime): Pushing config rollback now.
DeployBot: Change rolled out to runtime clusters: continuous_batching.window_ms=40, kv_prefix_cache.ttl=1800s. No errors reported.
Matt (sre): After rollback + scale, hotshard-3 GPU mem usage stabilized at ~78%, evictions stopped. Batching hit rate climbed to ~55%. Queue length down to 180.
Sara (support): Posted internal bulletin and notified affected customers. Some accounts seeing transient increased latency but no persistent errors.
Anna (oncall): Switching to monitoring mode. Oncall shift handoff: I'm tagging @Ravi for longer-term infra follow-up and @Lee for config postmortem. I'll remain as incident lead until 11:30UTC. Any blockers?
Ravi (infra): Need post-incident follow-ups: 1) request permanent GPU quota bump for eu-west-1, 2) revisit autoscaler backoff logic to fail fast on quota errors and try fallback, 3) add provider maintenance guard to capacity planner.
Lee (eng-runtime): Add item: run a canary for batching/window changes (simulate load) before rollout; add TTL change safety check to PR pipeline.
Matt (sre): I'll draft postmortem outline and own monitoring/alert tuning: trigger earlier on sustained cache miss rate + queue growth.
Anna (oncall): Great. Closing active mitigation. Incident severity: Sev2. Impact window: 10:12UTC - 10:28UTC. Owner: Matt (postmortem), Ravi (infra follow-up), Lee (runtime fix). Thanks all :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigation applied). Please follow the postmortem template in #postmortems when ready.
